title: CSS cascade, tokens, and component states
outcome: Explain why a style wins and build consistent states without escalating selector strength.
useCase: Shared components, themes, and regressions across screens.
drawbacks: System-wide changes need representative state checks.
version: Modern JavaScript / TypeScript · Vue 3.5 where applicable · browser APIs
cue: Inspect the winner. Name the choice. Test the state.

trace.title: Computed style
trace.detail: The cascade considers origin/importance and layers before specificity and source order. A more specific selector is not always the winner across different layers or important rules. Inspect the computed-style panel to see the actual winning declaration.

trace.title: Follow one item
trace.detail:
Select the element. Read computed style and the crossed-out rules. Locate origin/layer, selector, and source order. Remove accidental global leakage instead of adding another !important.

Then inspect every state in the same container and theme. Token changes need representative screens, long text, zoom, and focus checks. A contrast check is necessary for relevant colors; it does not test whether the task is understandable.

trace.title: Try the failure
trace.detail: A global button rule can break one nested form. Repeated !important patches make the next change harder. Color-only state is invisible to some users.
